question: Can historical wind speed/direction, rainfall, regional fire activity, satellite imagery and soil moisture improve Singapore's six-hour-ahead PM2.5 predictions beyond PM2.5-only baselines, especially during severe haze episodes?
study_area: Singapore receptor and source boxes A, B, C
interval: 2015-09-01 to 2015-10-31 (haze, main); 2016 clean season; 2019 held-out haze season; NEA before 2024-01-01
acceptance_criteria: Only inputs available at issue time enter the prediction experiment.
Inputs that M5 gated out or did not assess are excluded.
No supported gain is claimed from Stage P or one season.

limitations: Singapore PM2.5 is five NEA regions, not stations; the label start or end of hour is not stated.
Stage P results come from blocked folds inside one season and carry no skill claim.
The shift null in Experiment A has 31 shifts; no test can reach supported_association (Amendment 1).
Latencies for FIRMS, IMERG and SMAP are nominal values, not measured per file.
I1 ran on the 2015 season only. Other seasons of IMERG Early were not downloaded.
The 2015 negative ablation (30.76, 32.10, 36.73, 41.75) is a separate result and is not mixed with M5 numbers.
No causal attribution of Singapore PM2.5 to specific fires.
No operational forecast and no health advice.
No sealed NEA data (from 2024-01-01) was read.
Issue-time validity uses nominal product latency with an enforced input cutoff. The release time of each historical observation is not recorded.
Archived values can differ from the values published at the issue time.
Demonstration package outside the m41-v2 benchmark. It has no answer key and no score.
M5 computed every number in this package. The council reviews them and computed none.
FIRMS is the MODIS standard-product archive, not the near-real-time product. When each value was available at issue time is not known.
ERA5 is retrospective reanalysis. M5 used it only for association in hindsight.
HLS has 2.7% clear land on both pilot dates. SMAP has no recommended-quality retrieval in the study box. M5 gated out both.
2019 is the test season of both Stage T and M5-C. It was reused and is not an independent test. M5-C holds one 2019 episode.
